data.title: AI TRENDS | Big Tech Prioritizes AI Budgets Over Graduate Hiring
data.description: Satya Nadella said on a podcast that Microsoft has slowed hiring of recent graduates, with the company prioritizing staff reassignment and spending its AI budget before adding employees. According to PANews, Microsoft's full-time workforce declined by about 5,000 to 223,000 over a year, while revenue increased 18%. A study found that companies using Copilot reduced entry-level hiring by about 40%.

data.title: AguilaTrades Closes BTC Longs, Cuts Position by About $150 Million
data.description: AguilaTrades closed its BTC long positions, reducing its position by about $150 million. According to Odaily, it closed long positions totaling 2,440 BTC between 10:16 p.m. on November 27, 2026, and 5:52 a.m. on November 28, and currently has no BTC positions. Between 10:37 p.m. and 11:45 p.m. on November 27, it closed positions worth about $143 million, realizing a loss of about $3.34 million. Its net profit from BTC trades over the 30-day period from November 12 to 27, 2026, was about $10.88 million. The address is 0x1f250df59a777d61cb8bd043c12970f3afe4f925.

data.title: Anza Urges Immediate Agave Client Upgrade on Solana Mainnet
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Solana client development team Anza has urged node operators in a notice on the Solana mainnet to upgrade the Agave client to the latest version immediately. Anza said Solana’s clusters are operating normally. Jito-Solana and Harmonic have each released builds based on Agave v4.4.2, which node operators and validators can use to complete the upgrade.

data.title: Jailed Brazilian Beach Soccer Star Pulled Into Russia-US Spy Dispute
data.description: According to Bloomberg, a jailed Brazilian beach soccer star has become a bargaining chip in a dispute over an alleged Russian spy sought by both Moscow and Washington.

data.title: BinanceBlockchainWeek to Bring Industry Leaders and Law Enforcement Together
data.description: Binance announced on X that industry leaders, analytics experts and law enforcement will come together on one stage at #BinanceBlockchainWeek on Nov 28–29.

data.title: HSBC: Dollar and U.S. Equity Links Make FX Markets Harder to Read
data.description: According to Jin10, the dollar has benefited from safe-haven demand amid increased stock market volatility but is also sensitive to capital flows into AI-related trades, making market movements harder to interpret at times. HSBC Head of Digital Assets Research and Senior FX Strategist Daragh Maher said foreign exchange markets had shifted their focus from energy markets to equities. He said the dollar’s relationship with stocks was difficult to pin down because it serves as a safe-haven asset while also appealing as a proxy for “U.S. exceptionalism,” and the same stock market signal can prompt sharply different foreign exchange reactions.

data.title: U.S. Military Says It Struck Cargo Ship in Gulf of Oman, Leaving It Unable to Sail
data.description: According to Sina Finance, citing Xinhua, U.S. Central Command said on the 27th that U.S. aircraft struck a bulk carrier in the Gulf of Oman on the 26th, leaving it unable to sail. The ship was allegedly attempting to break through a U.S. Navy blockade.

data.title: Foreign Central Bank U.S. Treasury Holdings Fall by $47 Billion in Week Through November 20
data.description: According to Jin10, foreign central banks' holdings of U.S. Treasuries fell by $47 billion in the week through November 20, compared with a previous reading of $19.822 billion.

data.title: France's Finance Minister: S&P Says Budget Passage Is Urgent
data.description: According to Jin10, France's finance minister said S&P believes it is urgently necessary to ensure the budget bill is passed following its rating adjustment. France's economic outlook remains uncertain.

data.title: S&P Upgrade Brings South Africa Closer to Investment Grade
data.description: S&P Global Ratings raised South Africa’s credit rating for the second time in about a year, citing fiscal outperformance and an expected drop in government debt, Bloomberg reported. The upgrade moves the country closer to investment grade.

data.title: Nigeria Seeks 50% Remittance Growth to $1.5 Billion by 2027
data.description: Nigeria’s central bank aims to increase remittances from citizens living abroad by 50% next year, reaching $1.5 billion by 2027, to boost foreign-exchange reserves, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: World Liberty-Linked Wallet Converts WETH and mETH Into $20 Million in Stablecoins
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, a wallet linked to World Liberty converted its WETH and mETH holdings into approximately $20 million in stablecoins. After the transactions, its ETH, WETH and mETH balances were all zero. About 16.59 million USDC was transferred to the Dolomite lending protocol.

data.title: S&P: French Government Debt to Keep Rising, Interest Costs to Climb by 2029
data.description: According to Jin10, S&P said French government debt will continue to rise throughout the forecast period, while interest payments will gradually increase through 2029. France's persistent political polarization may continue to constrain the implementation of deficit-reduction measures and pro-growth reforms.

data.title: Binance Brasil Receives Third Brazilian License
data.description: Binance announced on X that Binance Brasil has received its third license in Brazil from the Central Bank of Brazil, authorizing it to operate as a foreign exchange broker. The company said the license is part of its commitment to compliance and improving financial products for local users.

data.title: ECB Vice-President Boris Vujčić: Market Expectations for the Next Rate Decision Likely to Materialize
data.description: According to Jin10, ECB Vice-President Boris Vujčić said he believes market expectations for the next rate decision are likely to come true, provided no surprises occur beforehand.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Prices Fall as Stock Rally Weakens Safe-Haven Demand
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. Treasury prices fell when trading resumed after the Thanksgiving holiday, as gains in stocks weakened demand for safe-haven assets. Yields across maturities rose 6 to 8 basis points, with the 10-year yield at 4.93%; yields were near session highs at Friday’s early close.

TD Securities strategist Prashant Newnaha said increased risk appetite was the main driver of the modest rise in bond yields. For weeks, the artificial intelligence trade has been a major influence on the Treasury market: gains in AI stocks have weighed on bond demand, and the reverse has also occurred. Whether hundreds of billions of dollars in AI spending generate returns matters for the U.S. economy and the Federal Reserve’s response to high inflation.

The latest move gave back some of Treasuries’ earlier gains, which had followed a stock sell-off driven by growing doubts about the AI trade and a reduction in traders’ bets on Fed rate hikes. Overnight index swaps showed a 100% probability of two Fed rate hikes by March next year and nearly a 90% chance of a third by midyear. Two weeks earlier, swaps indicated expectations for three hikes by September next year and a 35% chance of a fourth. Some traders now expect the Fed to shift toward easing later next year as the effects of rate hikes and falling stocks weigh on the world’s largest economy.

Jefferies economist Mohit Kumar said the Fed’s December policy meeting could mark the peak in hawkishness and a turning point for markets.

Technology shares stabilized on Friday. The Nasdaq 100 rose 2.6%, the S&P 500 gained 1.6%, and Nvidia rose 0.8% after falling as much as 2.6%.

At 2 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, the two-year Treasury yield was up 6.2 basis points at 4.7036%; the five-year yield rose 7.3 basis points to 4.742%; the 10-year yield gained 7.6 basis points to 4.9296%; and the 30-year yield increased 7.3 basis points to 5.3213%. The five-year/30-year spread was little changed at 57.75 basis points, while the two-year/10-year spread widened about 1.3 basis points to 22.39 basis points.

For post-holiday trading, the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association recommended a 2 p.m. New York close for dollar-denominated bonds. Bloomberg’s bond index used 1 p.m. prices for the day’s close, when U.S. stocks finished trading; CME interest-rate and stock-index futures ended trading 15 minutes later.

data.title: Capital Economics’ Jonas Goltermann: Flat Treasury Yield Curve Signals Tightening Risks
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Capital Economics Chief Market Economist Jonas Goltermann said the U.S. Treasury yield curve is at its flattest level since early last year. Short-term Treasury yields remain high relative to long-term yields, reflecting the market’s view that tight monetary policy will weigh on economic growth and corporate profits.

data.title: U.S. Crude Oil Futures Settle at $83.08 per Barrel, Down 60 Cents or 0.72%
data.description: According to Jin10, U.S. crude oil futures settled at $83.08 per barrel, down 60 cents, or 0.72%.

data.title: STOCKS | Anthropic Swings in First Trading Week, Closes Above $83 IPO Price
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Anthropic PBC ended its first week on Nasdaq above its $83 IPO price. Shares rose nearly 11% in New York on Friday to close at $91.88, their highest closing level since trading began on November 19, recovering after closing below the IPO price in each of the previous two sessions.

Risk appetite picked up after the Thanksgiving holiday, and Anthropic joined a broad advance in U.S. stocks. The company, led by Dario Amodei, had a market capitalization of about $1.7 trillion, below its peak of more than $2 trillion on its first trading day, when shares touched $115.10.
